country.name: Zambia

default_in_force_rule.text: Not applied: every version is dated by ZambiaLII's own expression date, the day the amendment it incorporates took effect as Laws.Africa records it. No date is computed from a default rule.

country.licence_note: Source: ZambiaLII (https://zambialii.org), licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International licence (CC BY-NC 4.0).

sources.name: ZambiaLII (Southern African Institute for Policy and Research, on the Laws.Africa Peachjam platform)
sources.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0, crediting ZambiaLII as the source (https://zambialii.org/terms-of-use/)
sources.notes: Point-in-time expressions of each act, /akn/zm/act/<year>/<num>/eng@<date>. ZambiaLII's document pages answer automated clients with a Cloudflare challenge, so each expression page is read from its latest Internet Archive capture (raw id_ form); the capture timestamps and sha256s are pinned in sources.json. Request count covers the Internet Archive and ZambiaLII's open listing pages.

sources.name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine
sources.licence: Archived copies of ZambiaLII pages; the content licence is ZambiaLII's
sources.notes: CDX API for discovery, then https://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<original url> for the page bytes.

decisions: Acts were chosen by what the archived source supports: every expression ZambiaLII lists for the Constitution (4), the Data Protection Act 2021 (1), the Lands Act (3) and the Anti-Terrorism and Non-Proliferation Act 2018 (3) has an Internet Archive copy, so each version is read from its own dated expression.

The Penal Code (Cap. 87) was not taken: ZambiaLII lists 11 expressions (1996 to 2023), but the Internet Archive holds only 2 (1996-12-31 and 2023-12-26), so nine amending Acts from 2000 to 2023 could only be dated 2023-12-26. It also lists the Penal Code (Amendment) Act 2026 (Act 75 of 2026) as an amendment not yet applied.
The Companies Act 2017 and the Employment Code Act 2019 were not taken: their archived ZambiaLII pages carry no Akoma Ntoso text (the LII shows only the source PDF), and no OCR is used.
The Insurance Premium Levy Act 2015 was tried and dropped: 2 of its 5 expressions (2018-01-01, 2022-01-01) have no usable archived copy, so two Acts' changes could only be dated a year late.
In the Constitution of Zambia Act, the Constitution itself is the Schedule (att_1); its articles are filed as art-NNN beside the Act's own sections (sec-NNN).

Licence and terms: ZambiaLII licenses its content CC BY-NC 4.0 with attribution, and its terms prohibit scraping and bulk downloading from its website; its robots.txt sends Content-Signal ai-train=no, ai-input=no and Crawl-delay 5, and its document pages answer automated clients with a Cloudflare challenge. No ZambiaLII document page was fetched: every version is read from the Internet Archive's copy, at most one archive.org request per 3 seconds, for the configured acts only. The user decided on 2026-10-28 that reading these archived copies is acceptable (relayed by the coordinator: "scraping wayback is fair game, dont overdo it"). The repository stays private; CC BY-NC allows only non-commercial use. No legal text was given to a model.
ai_use: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, claude-opus-5-5) wrote the adapter and configuration and chose the acts. No model wrote, summarised or transformed legal text: parse.py is deterministic code.
